findings.evidence: Pass `"$branch"` quoted. Single quotes are needed only for a literal name you type containing `$` (`'feature/weird$name'`), which the shell would otherwise expand.
findings.fix: Cut this to one clause or delete it. The model already knows how shell quoting works, and step 5 already quotes "$branch".

findings.evidence: If `$remote` is set and `git merge-base --is-ancestor "$remote" "$orig"` fails, the remote has commits the local branch lacks: stop
findings.fix: Add one decision check before any mutation: 'Before rebasing, ask whether anyone else pushes to this branch. If `git log --format=%ae "origin/$target..$remote"` shows authors other than the user, stop.' The description excludes shared branches, but the body never tells the agent how to spot one. Right now it only notices a shared branch when the remote has diverged.

findings.evidence: ## Gotchas lists three items, one of which (line 25) is generic shell quoting
findings.fix: Replace the quoting item with a gotcha from real use, for example: 'Stacked branches: rebasing a branch that other local branches build on leaves them on the old SHAs. Pass `--update-refs` (git 2.38+) or tell the user which dependent branches need rebasing.'

findings.evidence: If the lease is rejected, someone else pushed: stop, do not retry with `--force`.
findings.fix: Finish the lease-rejected branch: 'Report that the local branch is already rebased and was not pushed. Give the pre-rebase tip `$orig` and the recovery command `git reset --hard $orig`. Then list the new remote commits with `git fetch origin && git log --oneline "$branch..origin/$branch"`.' The agent should not leave the user with no next step.
